subject: Evaluation onboarding: success criteria, RACI, and sprint timetable
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@docuware.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0500
Subject: Evaluation onboarding: success criteria, RACI, and sprint timetable

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for a good discovery earlier. Per our call, I captured a compact plan so we can kick off the 3-week evaluation with clear success metrics and owner responsibilities. Please review and confirm edits below. If this looks good we’ll send a calendar invite for the kickoff and share the short checklist.

Key success criteria (must-have to consider trial successful):
- 2 representative flows integrated end-to-end (API -> app) with <= 300ms median inference latency for 95% of tokens (on your staging GPU config)
- Qualitative rating: Product team confirms outputs meet acceptance for the 4 test prompts in the evaluation doc (pass/fail)
- No PII leakage in sampled logs; audit traceability enabled for requests used in the eval
- Throughput: sustained 50 qps in the representative traffic pattern for 10 minutes without errors

Proposed RACI (high level):
- Infra (VPC + staging GPUs): Responsible — DocuWare infra lead (Sam); Consult — Naomi, Ben; Accountable — DocuWare CTO
- App integration (API wiring, sample prompts): Responsible — DocuWare app eng; Consult — Jordan; Accountable — DocuWare PM
- Security / data controls (logging, KMS, retention): Responsible — DocuWare security; Consult — Kimberly; Accountable — DocuWare CISO
- Redwood runbook (model pinning, routes, batching config): Responsible — Naomi/Ben; Consult — DocuWare infra; Accountable — Naomi
- Procurement / temporary credits & billing: Responsible — Jordan; Consult — DocuWare procurement; Accountable — Naomi

Timeline (target):
- Day 0 (kickoff): align scope, ship access, share checklist (this week)
- Day 1–4: infra setup + staging keys; Redwood shares baseline config and test harness
- Day 5–11: app integration + smoke tests; iterate on prompts
- Day 12–18: load/latency run, sampling, security review
- Day 19–21: final acceptance window; short readout

Attachments: I’ve attached a short onramp checklist and a draft evaluation metrics doc.

Next steps I can take: schedule kickoff (30–45m), create the short mutual action plan in HubSpot, and provision a temporary Dedicated slot for the runs.

Ask: please confirm who will be the primary infra contact and which staging region you’ll want us to use (us-east1 / us-west1).

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman | Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@docuware.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: eval@docuware.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Evaluation onboarding: success criteria, RACI, and sprint timetable

On Wed, Nov 4, 2026 at 4:12 PM Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sam —
>
> Thanks again for a good discovery earlier. Per our call, I captured a compact plan so we can kick off the 3-week evaluation with clear success metrics and owner responsibilities. Please review and confirm edits below. If this looks good we’ll send a calendar invite for the kickoff and share the short checklist.

Thanks Naomi — this is exactly the level of clarity we needed. Quick answers inline:
- We can own infra and staging GPUs (I’ll be the lead).
- Staging region: us-east1 preferred (closer to our test cluster).
- Security will run initial checks but will need a short list of expected log fields (timestamp, request id, prompt hash) — Kimberly, can you share?

Couple of asks from our side:
1) Can Redwood pre-configure a batching profile and a conservative quantized model variant so we can smoke-test latency before we wire app traffic?
2) We’ll need a statement of temporary credit usage/limits and whether there are any SLA exceptions for short load bursts.

We’re good to kick off tomorrow morning if you can do 10:00am ET.

—Sam
Sam Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, DocuWare

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Sam Torres <sam.torres@docuware.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 08:31:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Evaluation onboarding: success criteria, RACI, and sprint timetable

Looping in a couple of practical notes for the kickoff and to set expectations:

1) Temporary capacity and credits: Jordan, I’ll draft a one-page credit plan (limits, expiration, contact) and attach to the kickoff invite. We should keep it conservative: 200 GPU minutes / day for the first week and escalate if needed.

2) Batching/config: Naomi and I will pre-stage a conservative batching profile and a 4-bit quantized variant of the model that typically trades a small quality delta for ~2x cost reduction. We’ll label it "q4-safe" and mark it as fallback for load tests. That addresses Sam’s ask (1).

3) Security checklist: Kimberly — please share the minimal log fields and retention policy that satisfy your team so we can update the eval metrics doc prior to kickoff.

4) Kickoff time: 10:00am ET tomorrow works for me. Naomi — please send the calendar invite with the attached checklist and the Drive folder link.

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Action items captured for kickoff:
- Ben: attach credit plan to invite + approve temporary Dedicated slot provisioning (ACTION: Ben)

- Jordan: create the HubSpot mutual-action-plan record and capture acceptance gates (ACTION: Jordan)

- Sam / DocuWare: confirm infra lead and internal access windows (ACTION: Sam)

If anyone needs an earlier sync, ping me and I’ll do a 15m pre-kick. Otherwise see you all tomorrow.

Best,
Naomi
